messages:
Maria R.: heads up — canary rollout for model-serving (eu-west1) showed traffic-shift completed but ~40% of canary pods never passed readiness, getting 503s. gitops claims success. anyone seeing related quota/node issues?
Sahil: checking the rollout id now — can you paste the pipeline link? also which helm chart version?
Maria R.: https://git.company/repo/-/pipelines/3245 — chart v2.7.3. I saw a handful of `OOMKilled` then `CrashLoopBackOff` before the 503s. no obvious node drains in cluster events.
Jen: I pulled the cluster events — got repeated errors from kubelet about device plugin unable to allocate GPUs. gcloud returned quota errors earlier today: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Insufficient resources in region eu-west1 for requested resource.`, plus some `FAILED_PRECONDITION` for GPU attachments.
Kai: gitops reconciler logs show it applied the traffic-split change (weight -> 20%) at 12:02, then applied the canary rollout at 12:03. However the rollout health probe timeout was 60s and the progressive controller considered the step complete because traffic-level gate succeeded. Looks like our progressive delivery gate is only checking REST API traffic routing, not pod readiness/capacity.
Sahil: that explains it — traffic shifted before the actual backing capacity was stable. We need a precondition that validates node capacity (GPU allocatable >= requested) and pod readiness percent threshold before advancing weights.
Maria R.: agree. current helm values had `throttle_percent: 5` in staging but codegen bumped prod to 20 in the CI job. I wonder if the CI mutated values during the apply.
Jen: found in the gitops mutation logs — ops-automation applied a patch to increase batch size and throttle. snippet: ```yaml
canary:
  weight: 20
  max_unavailable: 1
  prechecks: []
```
Kai: ops-automation also didn't run the `capacity-check` plugin because the terraform drift detector flagged subnet usage high and short-circuited some plugins. so two things: terraform drift -> plugin skipped -> traffic gate blind to capacity.
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline 3245: automated rollback executed (run: rollback-3245, reason: unhealthy canary threshold). Details: https://git.company/repo/-/deploys/rollback-3245
Sahil: rollback bot saved us, but we should avoid the flip side where traffic already shifted and we only notice after rollback. Proposed fixes: add node-capacity precheck to progressive controller, gate traffic-shift on (pods_ready_percent >= X) AND (gpu_allocatable >= requested_count), increase canary probe timeout to 5m for first ramp, and make ops-automation not mutate `weight` without an explicit owner check.
Maria R.: also add a terraform plan guard: if subnet/gpu quotas are below threshold, fail the rollout early with a clear message. we had silent drift from a manual bootstrap that inflated subnet usage.
Jen: I'll open a quick PR to add capacity prechecks and a README for ops-automation mutation rules.
Kai: I'll add a GitOps reconciler check that refuses to flip traffic unless the progressive controller reports the new revision as Healthy. Also suggest adding a canary `safety_timeout` so the controller pauses if capacity signals are flaky.
Sahil: for short-term mitigation — reduce canary weight to 5% and extend step duration in prod, patching via `kubectl -n infra patch canary` now? Maria, want me to do it?
Maria R.: please do. and file an incident note so CS/escalations know why there was a brief degraded experience.
Jen: PR #482 opened: add capacity prechecks + doc.
Kai: created issue #987 to track terraform quota guard and ops-automation ownership checks.
Maria R.: thanks everyone — follow-ups: (1) Sahil patches canary weight (done), (2) Jen PR, (3) Kai reconciler guard, (4) Ops to run quota cleanup for eu-west1. saving lessons learned to the rollout runbook. :thumbsup:
Sahil: patch applied, canary back at 5% and probe timeout extended. monitoring cpu/gpu metrics for next 30m.
deploy-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026 — transient canary failure due to GPU quota drift (linked).
Maria R.: closing thread — please ping if anything else crops up. thanks. :white_check_mark:
